name: Siege of Antioch
summary: The First Crusade besieges Antioch from October 1097 to June 1098, a seven-month siege that tests the crusaders to the breaking point. The city is taken through treachery (Bohemund bribed a guard). Three days after the crusaders capture Antioch, a relieving Turkish army arrives; the crusaders are now besieged inside the city they just captured, facing starvation. The miraculous discovery of the 'Holy Lance' (supposedly the spear that pierced Christ's side) inspires a sortie that routs the Turkish army (June 28, 1098). Bohemund keeps Antioch and founds the Principality of Antioch.

_quarry.structural_significance: Creates the Principality of Antioch; demonstrates the tactical effectiveness of crusader morale even under extreme conditions; establishes the pattern of Crusader state formation from conquered cities
